rationale: The buyer is a specific, named technical role (startup CTO / ML engineer) evaluating a real commercial decision with money on the line — solid buyer clarity and genuine pain. Willingness to pay is reasonable given adjacent tools (Infracost, CloudZero) already monetize infrastructure cost visibility for engineers. However, the build_gate for willingness_to_pay (min 5) is met, but responsiveness_signal is essentially zero (single HN comment, no probe), and this topic moves fast — model pricing changes frequently, making the calculator stale quickly. Cap at validate until a landing page or waitlist confirms demand.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an LLM Inference Cost Calculator: a web form where a user inputs their model choice, expected token volume, and latency requirement, and gets back a side-by-side monthly cost estimate (self-hosted GPU vs. major API providers). The factory builds it as a Claude-powered calculation engine behind a simple static page with a Stripe payment link for a one-time report or a $29/month subscription tier — no coding by Youval. To sell, the factory drafts cold outreach to CTOs and ML engineers visible on LinkedIn or in AI startup communities (AngelList, YC forums) plus a Product Hunt launch post; all outreach batches go out only after Youval approves. Ongoing delivery is fully automated: user submits inputs → Claude computes the comparison → PDF/email report sent automatically; pricing data updates are a scheduled Claude task pulling public API pricing pages. The only recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing any edge-case refund requests.
notes: No build_gate failures. Responsiveness_signal is pre-test; validate with a landing page before committing to build.
